## Figure 1.15: Remittances, by Region, 2019–25
Bar chart

- **Units:** US$ (billion)
- **Y-axis:** 0 to 250
- **X-axis / time span:** 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025
- **Series / legend:**
  - Sub-Saharan Africa
  - East Asia and Pacific (excl. China)
  - Latin America and the Caribbean
  - Europe and Central Asia
  - Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan
  - South Asia

### Estimated values from bar heights
All values are approximate because no printed data labels are shown.

| Year | Sub-Saharan Africa | East Asia and Pacific (excl. China) | Latin America and the Caribbean | Europe and Central Asia | Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan | South Asia |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2019 | ≈50 | ≈86 | ≈96 | ≈48 | ≈80 | ≈116 |
| 2020 | ≈44 | ≈86 | ≈102 | ≈45 | ≈85 | ≈120 |
| 2021 | ≈49 | ≈91 | ≈129 | ≈54 | ≈97 | ≈124 |
| 2022 | ≈54 | ≈100 | ≈142 | ≈68 | ≈92 | ≈144 |
| 2023 | ≈56 | ≈107 | ≈152 | ≈62 | ≈80 | ≈157 |
| 2024 | ≈62 | ≈112 | ≈162 | ≈64 | ≈97 | ≈182 |
| 2025 | ≈51 | ≈110 | ≈162 | ≈69 | ≈111 | ≈205 |

### Visual ranking and comparisons
- **Largest in every year:** **South Asia**.
- **Second-largest in every year:** **Latin America and the Caribbean**.
- **Smallest most years:** **Sub-Saharan Africa**, except in **2025**, when it appears slightly below **Europe and Central Asia** and clearly below all other regions.
- **2025 ranking:** South Asia > Latin America and the Caribbean > Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan ≈ East Asia and Pacific (excl. China) > Europe and Central Asia > Sub-Saharan Africa.
- **Strongest growth over the period:** **South Asia**, rising from about **116** in 2019 to about **205** in 2025.
- **Latin America and the Caribbean** rises strongly from about **96** in 2019 to about **162** by 2024–25, then appears roughly flat between 2024 and 2025.
- **East Asia and Pacific (excl. China)** dips little or not at all in 2020 and then trends upward to about **110** by 2025.
- **Europe and Central Asia** grows notably from about **48** in 2019 to about **69** in 2025, with a small dip around 2023.
- **Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan** rises overall but is more volatile: up through 2021, down in 2022–23, then up again to about **111** in 2025.
- **Sub-Saharan Africa** is comparatively flat: around **50** in 2019, peaking around the low **60s** in 2024, then dropping back to just above **50** in 2025.
- No negative values are shown.

**Source:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
